t-rowA.text: 1 · Arriving — the collection, and a brand-new trip

legend.text:
HOW TO READ THESE

Lo-fi on purpose: greyscale, no brand colour, no type decisions. Judge structure only — what sits where, and what is loudest.

Solid box = ships in this redesign.
Dashed box = reserved slot, renders nothing until that feature lands (R2 settlement, R3 transport, R4 notifications, chat).
Grey block = cover image.

F/AC numbers refer to docs/specs/004-trip-ia-redesign.md.

decisions.text:
SETTLED 2026-11-10

D1 Four destinations: Overview · Plan · Money · Group
D2 Map is a mode, not a tab
D3 One assistant, not three AI surfaces
D4 Countdown starts at T-7
D5 Chat reserved, not in v1
D6 Desktop = segmented tabs
D7 Three build slices
D8 Covers land first

n-trips.text:
TRIPS LIST (F15, AC—)

Grouped Live now / Upcoming / Past, nearest first. No tab bar here: tabs belong to a trip, not to the collection.

The past card carries 'You owe €42 · Settle up'. That pill is the only reason anyone opens this app after a trip ends.

n-setup.text:
OVERVIEW · SETUP (F4, AC6, AC25)

Fixes A5: today a new trip shows five empty sections at once. Here it shows ONE job — invite the group — and three quiet secondary actions.

The four tabs are already present and carry no badges. Nav never changes shape, even when the trip is empty.

t-rowB.text: 2 · Overview adapts to the phase — the four tabs never move

n-planning.text:
PLANNING (AC20, AC22)

Top block is the open poll waiting on YOUR vote — the needs-me layer that fixes A7.

'Since you were away' is the activity log we already write server-side and have never shown (A10).

Plan tab carries badge 1.

n-countdown.text:
COUNTDOWN · T-7 (AC7, F18)

The job changes from deciding to being certain. Day-1 logistics go above the fold.

Two dashed slots: transport status (R3) and packing. They are drawn now so shipping R3 is 'fill the slot', not 'find somewhere to put it'.

n-live.text:
LIVE (AC8, AC17, D2)

A now screen, not a summary. Now/Next first, then where everyone is.

Add expense is one tap from the top — the only place F6 allows an open composer, because fast capture is the whole job here.

Map opens as a mode.

n-wrap.text:
WRAP (AC9, R2)

After the trip exactly one thing matters. Balance and Settle up are the first block — this is the home for the settlement work in the roadmap.

Everything else on this screen is memory, not task.

n-plan.text:
PLAN (F11, AC11-14)

Day-grouped itinerary — today's group is marked during Live.

Decisions (polls) live here: a poll is nearly always a question about the plan.

Ideas is the old AI essay, collapsed. It no longer sits in the header pushing the itinerary below the fold (A3).

Every create form is behind a button (F6).

n-planempty.text:
PLAN · EMPTY (F14, AC25)

The pattern every destination uses: one line saying what this is for, then the primary action, then the assistant as the low-effort path.

Four destinations on a young product feel empty without this. The empty states are not polish — they are what makes the structure survive.

n-money.text:
MONEY (F12, AC15)

Splitwise-shaped: your own position first, settle up as the primary action, then the trip total, then the ledger.

Today this information is at the bottom of a 10-section scroll, under a form. The server already computes settlements.

n-moneysettled.text:
MONEY · SETTLED (AC16)

When nothing is owed the screen says so plainly, with no red and no zero badge.

A debt UI that shouts when there is no debt trains people to ignore it.

n-group.text:
GROUP (F13, AC18-19, R4, D5)

Avatars and names replace the raw email addresses currently shown in presence, members, polls and expenses (A9).

Notification preferences land here (R4). Chat is a dashed slot — we cannot out-chat WhatsApp; our advantage is state, not stream.

n-map.text:
MAP MODE (F9, D2)

Full screen, entered and dismissed, Esc closes it. Not a fifth tab: live location is useful for ~2 days of a 60-day object.

The sharing state and its countdown are visible while the map is open, never buried in a settings screen.

n-assistant.text:
ASSISTANT (F10, D3)

Replaces three disconnected AI surfaces: auto travel suggestions, 'Generate with AI', and Ask AI (A8).

One contract: it drafts, the group decides. Every answer arrives as proposals with Add to plan / Dismiss.

The accuracy disclaimer appears once, here, instead of beside every list.

n-desktop-o.text:
DESKTOP · OVERVIEW (D6, N1)

The bottom tab bar becomes segmented tabs under the trip header, inside the existing 1100px container. Same four routes, same order, same badges.

A left rail only earns its place beyond five destinations, and we have capped it at four.

n-desktop-p.text:
DESKTOP · PLAN + MAP (D2, F9)

On a wide screen the map becomes a companion panel beside the itinerary rather than a full-screen takeover — the Wanderlog pattern. Same mode, more room.

It is still not a tab.
